newsitem.title: USA: Hearing set for Tuesday on Ill. incinerator bill.
newsitem.headline: Hearing set for Tuesday on Ill. incinerator bill.

text.p: An Illinois House committee will hold a hearing Tuesday on a bill that would restore a state subsidy to two bond-financed waste-to-energy incinerators.
The hearing before the House Public Utilities Committee will be held at 1400 EST in Springfield, according to the office of State Rep. Shirley Jones, D-Chicago, the committee's chairman.
While no list of speakers was available from Jones' office, environmental groups were expected to testify against the bill.
Those groups helped in the repeal last year by the Illinois General Assembly of a law that guarenteed incinerators a higher rate at which they could sell the electricity they produced to utilities.

The subsidy led developers to build or plan incinerators in at least four municipalities. Facilities financed with nearly $400 million of unrated, tax-exempt bonds were built in the Chicago suburbs of Robbins and Ford Heights.
Other projects were planned in Fulton, which sold $84.6 million of bonds, and Wood River, which had yet to sell any debt by the time the subsidy was yanked.

The bill, sponsored by State Rep. Harold Murphy, D-Markham, would only return the subsidy to the Robbins and Ford Heights projects because those incinerators had been financed, substantially completed and had received necessary government orders and permits.

Documents from the Environmental Law & Policy Center, a Chicago-based environmental advocacy group, indicated that returning the subsidy to the two incinerators would cost the state more than $700 million over a 20-year period.

Gov. Jim Edgar cited the high cost of the subsidy when he signed the repeal into law a year ago. A top aide to the governor has said it was "highly unlikely" Edgar would change his mind about the subsidy.
Murphy's bill will also be opposed by House Speaker Michael Madigan, D-Chicago, according to Madigan's spokesman Steve Brown.

Meanmwhile, incinerator developers, Foster Wheeler Corp, which built the Robbins incinerator, Polsky Energy Corp., the developer of the Wood River facility, and CGE Ford Heights and CGE Fulton have lawsuits pending in state courts challenging the subsidy's repeal.
